rounds.text: Nexome Capital Markets Ltd trades at an exceptionally low P/E of 9.59x [E1] and a P/B of 0.58x [E2], representing a steep discount compared to the broader sector benchmarks of 37.01x and 7.64x respectively [E6, E7]. This fundamental mispricing is further underscored by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value estimate of Rs 457 per share against a market price of Rs 115, leaving a massive margin of safety of 74.8% [E44, E45]. The reverse DCF model confirms that the current market price implies an unrealistic -1.1% earnings growth, while the business has actually demonstrated phenomenal profit expansion with a 193% CAGR over the last five years and a 1737% surge in trailing twelve months profit growth [E19, E21, E46]. Operational performance has experienced a dramatic inflection, highlighted by an operating margin reaching 39% in March 2026 compared to 1% three years earlier, alongside strong operating cash flow of Rs 11 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 9 Cr in the same period [E30, E35, E36]. Balance sheet health remains robust with a very low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x [E38], complemented by increasing promoter ownership to 51.81% [E41] and favorable tailwinds in the Financial Services sector [E75]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years is -6% [E15], debtor days have increased to 70.6 days [E65], and foreign institutional holding has declined over the period [E42].

Nexome Capital Markets Ltd trades at an exceptionally low valuation, marked by a price-to-earnings ratio of 9.59x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.58x [E2], representing a steep discount against sector benchmarks of 37.01x and 7.64x respectively [E6, E7]. This mispricing exists despite explosive underlying fundamentals, highlighted by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 193% [E19] and a staggering 1737% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21], vastly outpacing a 5-year share price growth of only 24% [E23]. Operating profitability has surged dramatically, with operating margins reaching 39% in March 2026 compared to just 1% three years prior [E30], backed by a robust financial position featuring a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x and Rs 9 Cr in free cash flow [E36, E38]. Furthermore, the company benefits from a supportive macroeconomic backdrop with the Financial Services sector positioned in a strong tailwind [E73, E75], while insiders signal conviction as promoter holding has increased by 6.44 percentage points to 51.81% [E41]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has contracted over recent medium-term periods, including -6% over 5 years and -4% over 3 years [E15, E16], alongside a low historical median return on equity of 2% over the last decade [E26].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 9.59x and a P/B of 0.58x [E1, E2], and promoter holding increased to 51.81% [E41]. However, that low valuation is entirely justified by a multi-year structural revenue contraction, evidenced by a 5-year compounded sales growth of -6% and 3-year sales growth of -4% [E15, E16]. The touted profit surge masks a chronically poor return profile, with a 10-year median ROE of just 2% [E26], a 3-year low ROE of 3% [E28], and a recent ROE of 8% flagged as a negative by the screen engine [E29, E72]. Furthermore, underlying operational efficiency is deteriorating rapidly as debtor days ballooned from 24.1 to 70.6 days and working capital days surged from 20.0 to 66.7 days [E65, E66]. Compounded by a catastrophic historical drawdown of -94.7% and high annualised volatility of 65.8% [E52, E53], the low multiple reflects severe, lingering operational risks rather than a simple mispricing.
